definitions.explanation: Something of exceptionally high quality, especially food or drink. Conveys that something is so good it stands out as extraordinary.

examples.japanese: このケーキは{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ。
{地元|じもと}の{魚|さかな}を{使|つか}った{刺身|さしみ}は{絶品|ぜっぴん}だった。
examples.english: The sashimi made with local fish was exquisite.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}コミで{広|ひろ}まった{絶品|ぜっぴん}グルメを{食|た}べに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to try the superb dish that spread by word of mouth.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used as a predicate: Xは{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ (X is superb). Also used as a modifier: {絶品|ぜっぴん}グルメ (superb cuisine), {絶品|ぜっぴん}スイーツ (exquisite sweets). Overwhelmingly used for food and drink in modern Japanese, though it can apply to other items of exceptional quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {絶品|ぜっぴん}グルメ: superb cuisine
- {絶品|ぜっぴん}スイーツ: exquisite sweets
- {絶品|ぜっぴん}の{味|あじ}: exquisite flavor
- {絶品|ぜっぴん}料理{りょうり}: outstanding dish
